text.p: Unilever Plc formally launched its operations in Croatia on Tuesday, saying it was committed to growth in the country and would use its base there as a springboard into the region.
"This move is a long-term one and it's a serious one," Unilever southern and central Europe director Fergus Balfour said at a reception.
Unilever has a representative office in Zagreb, but is now in talks which may lead to joint manufacturing ventures in Croatia.
It is also actively interested in the Bosnian market, country manager Marcel Kerkmeester told Reuters.
It has so far only introduced personal care and detergents onto the Croatian market, representing some 40 percent of its portfolio. Its food lines will be added later, Balfour said.

He said Croatia's relatively high per capita income and Western consumer habits had made it interesting for the Anglo-Dutch company, which has been heavily advertising products including Omo detergent and anti-perspirants on state television in recent months.

Kerkmeester said Unilever currently employs 22 Croats but that number is expected to rise given the company's ambitions to grow in the region. He declined to detail Unilever's Croatian sales. -- Caroline Smith, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
